title: Associated const equality conflicts with associated type equality
body:
I tried this code and it compiled: ```rust trait Trait2 {} trait Trait1 { const A: u32; type A; } impl, const N: usize> Trait2 for [T; N] {} fn main() {} ``` Then I tried this code and it didn't compile: ```rust #![feature(associated_const_equality)] trait Trait2 {} trait Trait1 { const A: u32; type A; } impl, const N: usize> Trait2 for [T; N] {} fn main() {} ``` ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.72.0-nightly (37998ab50 2023-06-11) binary: rustc commit-hash: 37998ab508d5d9fa0d465d7b535dc673087dda8f commit-date: 2023-06-11 host: aarch64-apple-darwin release: 1.72.0-nightly LLVM version: 16.0.5 ```
Backtrace

``` error: expected associated type bound, found constant --> src/main.rs:10:16 | 10 | impl, const N: usize> Trait2 for [T; N] {} | ^^^^^^ | note: associated type defined here --> src/main.rs:5:5 | 5 | type A; | ^^^^^^ error: could not compile `proba2` (bin "proba2") due to previous error ```

### Explanation Rust allows for associated const parameter and associated type parameter to have the same name. So, I expected there would be some way to disambiguate which one I'm referring to when setting the equality constraint but haven't found a way to do so. This problem is related to [Associated Const Equality](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/92827)
